r7-layout-default.title: Layout-default judgment call
r7-layout-default.imperative: Independently judge the retirement layout default (_LAYOUT_ADAPTER = _LAYOUT_OPTION_B): is it genuinely unbound-with-a-placeholder, or is it Option B bound with a comment saying otherwise? Is there a materially better shape? Record pass/fail with a finding stating the independent ruling.
r7-layout-default.finding: INDEPENDENT RULING: agree with the commander's provisional lean -- this is genuinely 'unbound with a placeholder,' not 'Option B, bound, with a comment saying otherwise.' Three properties, all independently verified, are what separate a real placeholder from a disguised decision: (1) reversal cost is zero today -- episodes/ holds only README.md, no real episode exists to migrate; (2) the switch is REAL, not decorative -- all 6 layout-dependent seams (5 named in EPISODE_STORE.md section 7 plus the implementer's honestly-flagged 6th, _new_episode_path) gate off one _LAYOUT_ADAPTER constant, and RetirementSeamTests/SurgicalDisputeTests flip it at runtime and exercise Option A end-to-end successfully -- a hypothetical seam would be one adapter; this is two, proven; (3) every branch is marked TODO(g4) and the module's own docstring plus EPISODE_STORE.md section 7 both state in prose that this is held for human ratification -- a reader cannot mistake it for a ratified choice. A CLI-exposed --layout flag would not be materially better: it adds configuration surface without removing the need for SOME default when unset, and no external caller invokes this outside tests today. One cheap, non-blocking refinement worth suggesting: a stderr note when the placeholder default is exercised (e.g. on every real write) would give future unattended callers (#305's capture wiring) a visible signal that they are running against an unratified layout, which the current silent default does not surface.

r8-wrong-answer.title: Wrong-answer class: author adversarial deltas
r8-wrong-answer.imperative: Per lesson:round-trip-tests-prove-artifacts-not-parsers, author NEW adversarial delta inputs (not just re-run the suite) designed to make the writer return a wrong answer: silent PASS on invalid (misfiled-field casing/whitespace variants, unknown field names, dispute on nonexistent/mechanical field, punctuation-only retire reason, duplicate ops, missing required key) and false FAIL on valid (long value, literal backslash-n text, unicode, lone CR, CRLF). Record pass/fail with concrete inputs tried and results.
r8-wrong-answer.finding: 17 of 19 authored adversarial probes returned the correct answer (rejected genuinely-invalid input, accepted genuinely-valid input) -- casing/whitespace-variant misfiled fields, unknown mechanical/agent-supplied field names, empty/whitespace-only statements, dispute on nonexistent assertion id, dispute on a mechanical-looking id ('run'), missing required keys, 5000-char single-line value, literal backslash-n AS TEXT, unicode, lone CR. ONE demonstrated SILENT-PASS-THEN-CORRUPT defect (see r8-finding-1, the top-ranked finding in REVIEW_RESULT): _reject_newline() only checks for the literal characters '\n' and '\r', but parse_episode() sections/fields the file using str.splitlines(), which Python treats as line-broken on a WIDER character set (\v \f \x1c-\x1e \x85 U+2028 U+2029). A statement containing U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) passes the guard and writes successfully, but the NEXT time that episode is touched by any op (parse -> mutate -> re-render), the content after the U+2028 is silently dropped -- demonstrated: submitted statement 'safe text\u2028- status: retired' round-trips to 'safe text', losing the tail with no error anywhere. This is exactly the injection-corruption class EPISODE_STORE.md section 7 names as the reason single-line enforcement exists, just via characters the guard's char-set didn't anticipate. Two lower-severity gaps also found: (a) top-level unrecognized keys on a create/retire/amend-assertion op (outside the mechanical/agent_supplied/diagnosis sub-dicts) are silently accepted and ignored -- not a data-corruption risk (unused), and apply_lessons_delta.py has the identical laxity, so not a regression; (b) a retire reason that is only punctuation ('---', '.') is accepted, which is arguably correct per the doc's literal 'non-empty reason' wording, not a bug.

r9-atomicity.title: All-or-nothing under partial failure
r9-atomicity.imperative: Verify C4 is real: does a delta whose LAST op is invalid truly leave earlier ops unwritten? Does the validate-then-write separation hold if a failure occurs during write (not just validation), e.g. an unwritable path? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r9-atomicity.finding: VALIDATION-time atomicity is real and demonstrated: (1) suite's own AllOrNothingAtomicTests with last-op-invalid confirmed passing; (2) own probe: a valid op followed by a structurally-invalid op on a CRLF-containing pre-existing file (simulating a Windows autocrlf checkout) leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged including the CRLF bytes, both for a purely-structural rejection and for an apply-time rejection (op references a nonexistent episode) -- validate_delta() is pure (no disk I/O) and apply_delta()'s per-op loop only mutates in-memory Episode objects via tx.load()/tx.create(), deferring every disk write to one commit() call at the very end, so a failure ANYWHERE in the op loop (last op or not) leaves disk state untouched. WRITE-PHASE atomicity does NOT hold, and I demonstrated the gap directly: _Transaction.commit() (scripts/apply_episode_delta.py ~684-690) iterates writes.items() and calls path.write_text() once per touched file with no staging/rollback -- monkeypatching Path.write_text to fail on the 2nd of 2 writes (simulating a real OS-level failure: disk full, permission denied, a locked file) leaves the FIRST file's write landed on disk while apply_delta() still raises and returns exit 1 to the caller. This is a genuine, demonstrated defect: a multi-episode-touching delta that fails partway through the WRITE phase (as opposed to the validation phase) leaves a real partial write on disk, contradicting the module docstring's own unconditional claim ('applies them mechanically, all-or-nothing... leaves the store byte-for-byte unchanged') and the store's core concurrency rationale. The validate-then-write SEPARATION is real and complete; what's missing is making the WRITE step itself atomic (e.g. write every touched file to a temp path first, then rename all into place only once every write has succeeded, or stage to a scratch dir and move as a batch).

r10-test-quality.title: Test suite quality
r10-test-quality.imperative: Judge whether the 18 tests in tests/test_episode_store.py are genuinely adversarial or mostly happy-path with a few negatives. Identify any test that asserts something that cannot fail. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r10-test-quality.finding: Genuinely adversarial, not mostly happy-path: of 18 tests, 11 assert a REJECTION (misfiled field x2, mechanical-field-under-agent-supplied, missing required kind, unknown mechanical field, missing/absent retire reason x2, newline-injection fixture, newline in statement, newline in amend history, explicit-id-in-create) and the remaining 7 assert positive structural properties that would genuinely fail under a regression (byte-identical sibling assertion across a dispute, mechanical/retirement sections untouched by a dispute, retire's field diff matches the worked example with the file NOT moving under Option B, the Option-A adapter actually moving the file, amend resolving through resolve_episode_path under Option A on a retired episode, sequence-increment producing distinct filenames, the two-op atomicity tests). No test found that asserts something structurally incapable of failing -- each positive assertion targets a specific rendered string/byte-range that a plausible regression (e.g. re-ordering fields, touching a sibling, eager-commit) would visibly break, and the implementer's own report documents proving several of these red first by temporarily disabling the guard (verified: no TEMP-DISABLED markers remain in the shipped code). Gaps not covered by the suite (found by r8/r9's own probes, not the suite): the U+2028-class line-boundary character, and write-phase (as opposed to validation-phase) atomicity. Recommend both gaps get regression tests added when r8/r9's findings are addressed.

consolidation.summary: 8/8 close criteria (C2-C8, C7) hold under normal operation and independent reproduction. Layout-default placeholder judged genuinely unbound (concur with commander's provisional read). BLOCKING: two demonstrated (not hypothetical) wrong-answer defects -- (1) the C3b newline guard checks only literal \n/\r, but the writer's own parser (str.splitlines()) treats a wider character set (notably U+2028/U+2029) as line boundaries; a value containing one passes the guard, writes successfully, then is SILENTLY TRUNCATED the next time the episode is touched by any op -- demonstrated data loss with no error anywhere; (2) _Transaction.commit() writes multiple touched files sequentially with no staging/rollback, so an OS-level failure partway through a multi-file commit leaves an earlier file's write landed on disk -- demonstrated via a forced write failure on the 2nd of 2 writes. Both are narrow, mechanical fixes (broaden the newline guard to len(value.splitlines())>1; stage writes to temp paths and rename/commit as a batch) but both contradict the module's own all-or-nothing/single-line guarantees as currently implemented.
